prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Dark warm charcoal background, copper honeycomb carbon sheets, restrained teal arrows, cream readable labels. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show mechanical exfoliation. Left: thick graphite stack made of many honeycomb sheets. Middle: translucent adhesive tape curls upward lifting a thin top sheet from that stack, a clear peeling front. Right: a small thin honeycomb flake resting on a flat substrate. Exact stage labels: "Graphite", "Peel with tape", "Thin flake". No liquid.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 1536x1024 educational illustration for a dark graphene science website. Dark warm charcoal background, copper honeycomb carbon sheets, restrained teal arrows, cream readable labels. Three left-to-right stages, ample spacing, realistic dimensional scientific illustration, not a chart. Carbon sheets must be hexagonal honeycomb networks, never square grids. Short labels only, no other text. Conceptual, not operating instructions. Show oxidation-assisted exfoliation then reduction. Left: stacked graphite honeycomb layers. Middle: separated honeycomb sheets with teal oxygen-containing group markers attached, with a small label "Oxidise + exfoliate" above connecting arrow. Right: sheet with fewer teal markers and a few irregular holes, conveying reduced graphene oxide retains defects. Exact main labels: "Graphite", "Graphene oxide", "Reduced graphene oxide". Small arrow label between middle and right: "Reduce". Preserve copper carbon network; teal markers represent oxygen groups, not extra carbon.

Middle: cutaway converging-diverging nozzle with narrow throat and widening outlet; streamlines travel left to right, stacked particles carried through. Above nozzle show a large circular magnified conceptual inset of gas pushing copper honeycomb layers sideways with one separating, thin teal arrows along sheet surfaces.
